title: VERA-V: Variational Inference Framework for Jailbreaking Vision-Language Models
claim: Prior attacks build fixed one-shot inputs and get refused; ours learns a prompt distribution refined by judge feedback and succeeds.
layout: 2 stacked panels, left-to-right flow, feedback loop arrow returning from judge
description: Two stacked gray panels share a raw-query bar on the left. The top panel, CS-DJ, runs left to right. A query is decomposed into three sub-queries, and each is rendered as a typographic sub-image. These are combined with distractor photos and a prompt text block, then sent to a red Target VLM that answers 'Sorry, I can't assist'. This panel is labeled 'One-Shot Attack Generation'. The bottom panel, VERA-V, starts with an Attacker LLM that learns a prompt distribution. It splits into a textual query and an image query. Typographic rendering and a diffusion model produce a typographic image and a generated image. These are merged with distractors and text, then sent to a red Target VLM that complies. A blue Judge Model sits above the VLM and sends a long feedback arrow back to the attacker. The red VLM boxes draw the eye first.
caption: Single-attack vs. feedback-driven multimodal jailbreak frameworks. Existing approach CS-DJ [ref] decomposes harmful queries into typographic sub-images and distractors, producing fixed, one-shot adversarial inputs. In contrast, VERA-V employs an attacker LLM that learns a joint text-image prompt distribution, refines it through optimization with judge feedback, and can subsequently sample diverse adversarial prompts during test time.
abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) extend large language models with visual reasoning, but their multimodal design also introduces new, underexplored vulnerabilities. Existing multimodal red-teaming methods largely rely on brittle templates, focus on single-attack settings, and expose only a narrow subset of vulnerabilities. To address these limitations, we introduce VERA-V, a variational inference framework that recasts multimodal jailbreak discovery as learning a joint posterior distribution over paired text-image prompts. This probabilistic view enables the generation of stealthy, coupled adversarial inputs that bypass model guardrails. We train a lightweight attacker to approximate the posterior, allowing efficient sampling of diverse jailbreaks and providing distributional insights into vulnerabilities. VERA-V further integrates three complementary strategies: (i) typography-based text prompts that embed harmful cues, (ii) diffusion-based image synthesis that introduces adversarial signals, and (iii) structured distractors to fragment VLM attention. Experiments on HarmBench and HADES benchmarks show that VERA-V consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on both open-source and frontier VLMs, achieving up to 53.75% higher attack success rate (ASR) over the best baseline on GPT-4o. We include the code on the project page available here: https://github.com/kxwhiowo/VERA-V
